citations.quote: The comparisons used to determine the greatest value are made according to the rules for simple conditions
in which case it shall not be rounded and all 32 digits shall be used
The result shall be the exact quotient truncated to 32 significant digits

cases.reason: The words match apart from the clause referred to (8.8.4.1 in 2002, 8.8.4.2 in 2023), which covers the same relation-condition comparisons. Under 2002 standard arithmetic, though, an argument that is an arithmetic expression is a 32-digit standard intermediate, and comparisons among intrinsic-function arguments use those 32 digits. Under 2002 rules, 1/K*K (K=3) and .9999999999999999999999999999999 + .0000000000000000000000000000009/10 are both 32 nines, so MAX should return the leftmost, which equals b. The compiler computes the first at 34 digits and returns it, so (MAX(b a) - b) * 10**33 prints 9.90 where 2002 gives 0.00. This is the known PB5575 34-digit defect reaching this rule.
cases.needs: its own verdict: the compiler's behaviour at --std 2002 for standard-arithmetic expression arguments is 34-digit (sel_std32.cob MAX-minus-b= 9.90, 2002 expects 0.00); re-probe after PB5575's run-time arm (on main, not in the pinned tree)

citations.quote: The equivalent arithmetic expression is as follows
the returned value shall equal the value of the equivalent arithmetic expression
The result shall be the exact quotient truncated to 32 significant digits
The equivalent arithmetic expression is as follows

cases.reason: The words are the same; only the subscript markup differs. What the equivalent expression means under standard arithmetic depends on the edition's arithmetic: 2002 uses a 32-digit truncating standard intermediate, while 2023's standard-decimal uses 34 digits. In 2002, MEAN(1 2 2) = 5/3 = 1.6666666666666666666666666666666 (32 digits), so (MEAN*3-5)*10**31 = -2. The pinned tree prints 0.01, a 34-digit, rounded value. mean_std32.cob also shows the COMPUTE transfer failing to round to 31 digits (§2002:8.8.1.3.1.3 GR3): it prints ...666 where 2002 gives ...667.
cases.needs: its own verdict: the compiler's behaviour at --std 2002 under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD is (MEAN(1 2 2)*3-5)*10**31 = 0.01, where 2002 requires -2.00; the PB5575 remainder covers the intrinsic bodies

cases.reason: Two 2002 reaches the 2023 row cannot show. (1) Communication reach, as q-40 found for LOG/MEAN/MAX: a 'data item of category numeric' in 2002 includes the implicit CD data-names (TEXT LENGTH, MESSAGE COUNT), whose category comes only from Annex A, and the alphanumeric STATUS KEY, which is refused. Probe at --std 2002 (CORRECT): la_cd.cob gives LA-LEN=0, LA-COUNT=0 and LA-CDREC=-999 for a numeric item in a CD record; la_cd_neg.cob refuses LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC(IN-STATUS) with COBOL1516. The CD program is refused outright at --std 2023 (COBOL0902), so the 2023 row's evidence cannot include it. (2) The reader's evidence item 'legal numeric and numeric-edited items accepted' is false at 2002. A floating-point numeric-edited item PIC -9.99E+999 is a legal argument under 2002 AR1 (2002 allows a picture exponent up to +999, 13.16.38.3 GR12) and no 2002 rule restricts it. The compiler refuses it at --std 2002 under native arithmetic (the default) with COBOL1660, citing §2023:15.58.4 r1, a 2023-only restriction (see 2002-RV-15.46.3-1). The 2023 argument set is narrowed by 2023 AR2, AR3 and RV1, none of which exists in 2002. needs: a 2002 witness for CD implicit data-names as argument-1 (candidate la_cd.cob / la_cd_neg.cob), and a fix of the COBOL1660 edition gate (see RV row). compiler-at-2002: correct for the CD reach, wrong for the floating-edited argument.

cases.reason: 2023 places a restriction on argument-1 beside this rule that 2002 does not have: §2023:15.58.4 RV1 requires a signed floating-point numeric-edited argument's negative extreme to pass IN-ARITHMETIC-RANGE, and 2023's RV2 (the pointer) governs only what is left. 2002 RV1 governs every numeric-edited argument, including PIC -9.99E+999 (legal in 2002: the picture exponent may be +999, 13.16.38.3 GR12). The 2023 verdict says nothing about those arguments. The compiler applies the 2023-only rule at --std 2002: la_bigexp.cob (native arithmetic, the 2002 default per 8.8.1.2) is refused with 'COBOL1660 ... outside the native (binary64) intermediate's range ... (ISO §2023:15.43.4 r1 / §2023:15.58.4 r1)' at --std 2002, for both PIC -9.99E+999 and -9.9(30)E+999. Under 2002 ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD the same argument is accepted and returns -9.99E+999 (la_bigexp_std.cob), which fits 2002's standard intermediate range of 9.999...E+999 (8.8.1.3.1.1). 2002 15.3.1 makes the representation of a native returned value implementor-defined, but no 2002 text licenses refusing the program. Secondary reach: the implicit CD data-names (TEXT LENGTH, MESSAGE COUNT) whose picture, and so whose lowest value, comes only from Annex A (la_cd.cob: 0 and 0, correct). needs: its own verdict: at --std 2002 under native arithmetic, LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC of a floating-point numeric-edited item whose extreme exceeds binary64 is refused with COBOL1660 (a §2023 rule); 2002 has no such restriction. The sibling is HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC (§2023:15.43.4 RV1, same COBOL1660 gate), which is not in this slice. compiler-at-2002: wrong.

cases.reason: 2002's blanket alphabetic rule, which 2023 removed (the cause q-39 found for LOCALE-DATE): §2002:8.5.2.1 lets an alphabetic item be specified wherever an elementary alphanumeric item is permitted as an operand, and treats it as alphanumeric where it is not expressly permitted. So in 2002, when argument-1 is alphanumeric, a PIC A(3) VALUE 'EUR' argument-2 is a permitted item treated as alphanumeric, which satisfies 'the same class as argument-1'. 2023 8.5.2.2 has no such sentence (2014 E.2 records the removal). The compiler refuses it at --std 2002 with 'COBOL1627: FUNCTION NUMVAL-C argument-2 is of class alphabetic; ISO §2023:15.3 requires ...' (nvc_alpha_a2.cob). Expected at 2002: accepted, with NUMVAL-C(' EUR 1,234.56', CA) = 1234.56. needs: its own verdict: at --std 2002 an alphabetic argument-2 is refused with COBOL1627 where 2002 8.5.2.1 permits it. compiler-at-2002: wrong.

cases.reason: This has the same 2002-only cause as AR-15.55.2-2. Sub-item a) governs 'If argument-1 is alphanumeric', and in 2002 an alphabetic argument-1 is permitted where AR1 asks for category alphanumeric and is treated as alphanumeric (§2002:8.5.2.1; 15.2 argument type 2 also admits class alphabetic). So the 2002 non-LOCALE format rule governs PIC A arguments, which the 2023 rule (no blanket rule) does not reach. The compiler refuses an alphabetic argument-1 at --std 2002 with COBOL1627 citing §2023:15.3 (nvc_alpha_a1.cob). Secondary point (doubtful only): the 'currency' element matches 'the default currency sign', and with CURRENCY SIGN 'EUR' only, 2002 counts one currency string where strict 2023 (SR25's implied '$') counts two (the q-41 deferral on AR4). The compiler matches 'EUR' and rejects '$' identically at both editions (nvc_cursign.cob), and no row test exercises a SPECIAL-NAMES currency without argument-2. needs: its own verdict: at --std 2002 an alphabetic argument-1 in the non-LOCALE form is refused where 2002 permits it; plus a 2002 witness for a SPECIAL-NAMES currency string (candidate nvc_cursign.cob). compiler-at-2002: wrong.

cases.reason: This is the LOCALE twin of AR-15.55.2-5. Item b) 2 governs 'If argument-1 is of category alphanumeric', and in 2002 an alphabetic argument-1 is permitted and treated as alphanumeric (§2002:8.5.2.1), so the LOCALE matching rules reach PIC A arguments in 2002 and not in 2023. The compiler refuses NUMVAL-C(SA LOCALE) with SA PIC A(5) at --std 2002 with COBOL1627 citing §2023:15.3 (nvc_alpha_loc.cob). The reader's other points hold: the ANYCASE fold in 2023 item 3 is one way of being case-insensitive, and EC-LOCALE-MISSING is observed at 2002 by pb64t6. needs: its own verdict: at --std 2002 an alphabetic argument-1 with LOCALE is refused where 2002 permits it. compiler-at-2002: wrong.
